newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Patria report rates Czech IPS shares a buy.
newsitem.headline: Patria report rates Czech IPS shares a buy.

text.p: Shares in Czech construction company IPS Praha a.s. are rated a buy as the company is well placed to profit from an expected boom in housing construction, investment bank Patria Finance said in a report to investors.
"We consider IPS a very promising company with a strong market position and excellent growth potential," it said.
"Its P/E ratio of 18.9, only slightly above the industry average, still provides a good investment opportunity. We recommend to buy the stock."
On Wednesday, IPS's share price on the Prague Stock Exchange (PSE) closed down one crown to 271.

During 1996 IPS underwent a number of structural changes including a merger with three small, wholly-owned subsidiaries and the purchase of one of the country's two largest railway construction companies -- Zeleznicni Stavitelstvi Praha a.s.(ZSP).
IPS also conducted a 10-for-one stock split on October 31 of this year. All the changes taken together give IPS a registered share capital of 1.4 billion crowns.
Patria said IPS was in a particularly good position to take advantage of the construction boom on two fronts: the railways and housing.
"The acquisition of ZSP has put IPS in the position of a domestic railway construction leader, benefiting from extensive government infrastructure spending," the report said.

"The company enjoys a particularly strong position in the Prague area where, housing construction should start to boom first. IPS expects to attain net profit margins above 10 percent in its real estate development projects," it added.
Construction output in the Czech Republic rose by a real 5.5 percent, year-on-year, over the January-October period.
IPS posted a consolidated pre-tax profit of 214 million crowns for the first nine months of 1996, a year-on-year increase of 18.7 percent.
